videos.title: Competition video for the judges
videos.audience: The judges: what was built tonight and why it matters, in one pass.
before: Run npm run check, then make one clean voice call (Power points card) and leave its transcript and summary on the Talk to Jane tab
Tabs open in this order: Architecture, Triage board, Talk to Jane, Portal
Claude Desktop open on a new chat, Harbourline tools set to Always allow
Screen recorder framed on the browser only, notifications off

steps.do: Start on the System architecture diagram. Point left to right: channels (including the voice agent), Airtable, the triage agent, the board, then Claude Desktop.
steps.say: Harbourline is a seven-person property manager in Brisbane. Maintenance comes in by phone, now answered by our voice agent, and by web form, email and text. Every Monday someone sorts it by hand, so the gas leak gets buried under a dripping tap. Tonight I built this: every channel lands in one Airtable base, Claude triages each request, and a person approves every message. Property managers can also ask about all of it in Claude Desktop, through MCP.
steps.task: Explain the problem and the architecture

steps.do: Walk the weekend's cards from the top. Open the gas card's Details for a second.
steps.say: Here's the weekend, triaged. The gas leak is at the top, and it noticed the after-hours transfer was never answered. It caught a duplicate across two channels, a repeat aircon fault, and it refused to guess which unit 8 a text meant.

steps.do: Show the earlier call's transcript and two-sentence summary.
steps.say: Tenants can also just ring Jane, our voice agent. Here's a call from earlier, with Claude's summary.
steps.task: Discuss maintenance job with voice agent

steps.do: Point to that call's Voice card: Urgent, Repeat fault, HPM-1207.
steps.say: Make.com dropped the call into the same Airtable base, and it was triaged like everything else: matched to the property, and flagged as a repeat electrical fault.
steps.task: Review job details on the board

steps.do: Live: copy the sample address and description, attach the sink photo, submit. Let the counter run.
steps.say: Now a new request, live, with a photo. The photo goes only to Claude and is never stored.

steps.do: The new Portal card lands. Open Details: photo description, tenant reply, work order.
steps.say: Matched to the property, urgency set from the photo, reply and work order drafted. Nothing is sent: a property manager approves every message.
steps.task: Review job details on the board
Query the jobs through MCP in Claude Desktop
steps.do: In a new chat (Harbourline tools set to Always allow), type: Find the property at unit 8. Which one is it? Let the table of eight properties appear, then stop.
steps.say: The same data is in Claude Desktop through an MCP server, and it still won't guess which unit 8. Built tonight with Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, from an empty folder, and it runs on Sonnet, so a small agency could afford it every day.

videos.fallback: If the live submit fails, cut to a portal request submitted a few minutes earlier, or re-record that segment.

videos.title: Platform walkthrough for a partner
videos.audience: A partner seeing the platform for the first time: what each part does, how they connect, and how it was built. Talk it through; the points below are prompts, not a script.
before: Run npm run check so the board has the 8 weekend requests
Tabs open: Architecture, Reports (Airtable), Triage board, Talk to Jane, Portal, Guide
A terminal in the practice folder for npm run check
Claude Desktop open with a new chat, Harbourline tools set to Always allow
sink-leak-photo.jpg ready; microphone allowed; quiet room

steps.do: Open on the System architecture diagram.
points: The problem: a seven-person Brisbane agency, requests by phone (now answered by Jane, our voice agent), web form, email and text, sorted by hand every Monday
The idea: every channel lands in one place, Claude triages, a person approves
Everything is fictional: Harbourline, the properties, the tenants (references only, like T-5010)

steps.do: Trace the diagram left to right.
points: Channels: the tenant portal, Jane the voice agent (Vapi) on the phone line, plus email, text and tradie reports
Make.com takes Jane's end-of-call report and writes a Requests row
Airtable is the source of truth: Properties (351), Maintenance jobs (183), Tradies (8), Requests
The triage agent: Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, about 10 seconds a request
The board for the property managers, and Claude Desktop: through the MCP server, property managers can ask about all of it (properties, jobs, tradies, requests) in plain English

steps.do: Switch to the Skills map tab.
points: How the AI Adoption Series skills map onto Harbourline
The triage procedure is the same written procedure as the course's maintenance-triage skill

steps.do: Show the Interface, then the base's tables.
points: Overview: open jobs by urgency and category, cost of completed jobs, Requests by urgency
The data is loaded exactly as given, including deliberate errors (HPM-1201 appears twice)
Requests is where every channel lands, with status New until triaged

steps.do: Walk the weekend's cards from the top, opening Details on two or three.
points: Emergency first, newest first within each urgency; times always in Brisbane time
02 gas: Emergency, and it noticed the after-hours transfer was not answered; no gasfitter on the list, so it says so rather than inventing one
06 unit 8: Emergency because the door can't be locked, but eight properties have a unit 8, so it asks for a call back
05 power points: an existing job, J-7050, open since 1 August; chase Brightline; the rent threat goes to things to confirm
03 and 04: the same tap by web form and by phone, caught as a duplicate
07: not maintenance, routed to Grace; 08: a tradie report that updates J-7302 and flags the leak from the unit above
Details: tradie, things to confirm, tenant reply, work order or landlord approval, original request; Triaged by Sonnet 5.5
steps.task: Review the weekend's jobs, card by card

steps.do: Use the filters: urgency, flags (Call back, Repeat fault), date, property address.
points: Showing X of Y requests updates as you filter
The address box searches both what the tenant typed and the matched property's address

steps.do: Run npm run check and let it finish (about 90 seconds; talk over it).
points: How triage works: code finds the property and its history, code applies the hard rules, one Claude call drafts the triage, code saves it
Hard rules in code: never guess a property, only tradies from the list, over 500 dollars needs the landlord's approval
The answer-key check: the 8 weekend requests reloaded and asserted in code, no AI judging AI; 23 checks
steps.task: How triage works: the answer-key check

steps.do: Live call: read the Power points sample card, answer Jane's questions, hang up. Then switch to the board.
points: Live transcript as you speak; a two-sentence summary from Claude at the end, display only
Make.com writes the call to Airtable; the board picks up the New row and triages it within about 20 seconds
Expect Urgent, a repeat fault, HPM-1207 - 69 Lakeside Ct, Toowong
steps.task: Discuss maintenance job with voice agent

steps.do: Submit the sink sample with the photo, then open the new card on the board.
points: The photo is shrunk in the browser, sent only to Claude, never stored; only a one-line description is saved
The reply is a draft: nothing goes to the tenant until a person approves it

steps.do: Ask: Find the property at unit 8. Which one is it? Then: What's still open at 69 Lakeside Ct, Toowong? Draft a chase to the tradie.
points: The MCP server gives Claude Desktop the same data: find a property, job history, open jobs, tradies
It never guesses a property, and it flags tenancy-law points to check with the RTA rather than stating them
steps.task: Ask Harbourline questions in Claude Desktop

steps.do: Show the Demo tab's Brought vs built card.
points: Brought: the written spec, the sample data, Jane's voice agent, the accounts
Built from an empty folder with Opus 5.5 in Claude Code: two tabs, five prompts, about 40 minutes
Runs on Sonnet at low effort, so the running cost suits a small agency

videos.fallback: If the live call or portal misbehaves, keep recording and show the earlier Voice or Portal card instead; it is a walkthrough, not a performance.
